dossier.architecture: Turreted adjustable-hood scorer with protected pneumatic four-bar collector and staged traversal climb.

subsystems.drivetrain: Drive architecture requires a separate technical reference; this walkthrough concentrates on mechanisms.
subsystems.intake: Compliant four-bar collector; actuator orientation protects cylinder rods in the deployed pose.
subsystems.transfer: Belt centering, two cargo sensors and operator-controlled rejection; LEDs show capacity and mode.
subsystems.scoring: Printed turret base, adjustable hood and differentiated wheel speeds; soft/hard target lock modes.
subsystems.endgame: Elevator, passive retaining hooks and pneumatic pivot repeatedly transfer to the next rung.
subsystems.controls: Automated climb and mode feedback reduce operator work.

versions: Added metal retention plates and anti-pinch flaps; shooter structure revised to meet mass budget.
dossier.analysis: Team distinguishes qualification RP needs from playoff scoring opportunity: with two reliable partner traversals, staying out to score can be preferable. This is a marginal-value decision, not a blanket rule.
limits: Only published/reviewed configurations are established; further intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.title: 2022-176 · A productive scorer may rationally skip the climb in some playoff roles
context_documents.body:
# 2022-176: A productive scorer may rationally skip the climb in some playoff roles

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A compliant four-bar collector and belt centering feed a turret/hood launcher. Capacity indicators and operator rejection coordinate cargo state. The automated climb is contrasted with continuing to shoot.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly says two partners capable of traversal can make continued scoring preferable in playoffs, while qualification bonus needs may require its climb.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Climb value is marginal and alliance-specific even in a season where climbing is generally important. This is not evidence that the 2022 climb was universally irrelevant, nor justification for projecting its value into 2026.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Compare expected scored cargo during the whole climb interval with climb reliability, partner capability and qualification RP needs.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/rfqTnel-P8U](https://youtu.be/rfqTnel-P8U)

source_reviews.title: Behind the Bumpers with Aces High at Championship
source_reviews.locator: 1:33–3:44 intake; 3:45–6:12 indexing; 6:15–9:04 turret; 9:10–11:18 climb and allocation
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the full available English automatic caption track, including the start and end. Technical details are attributed to team speakers. No visual inspection claimed.
facts: Metal plates reinforce bearing retention in stressful areas and flaps address cargo pinching.
Two motor-driven centering belts feed a tunnel. LEDs show capacity, wrong-color state and climb mode.
The elevator starts at the middle bar and transfers load to latching hooks while pneumatic pivot changes its reach.
source_reviews.limitations: The turret travel description is qualified by a hose stop in the same passage. No measured shot or climb reliability sample.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Aces High used a compliant intake for contact with the field and a controlled, centered path into its shooter. The team spent design effort at both ends of the cycle: keeping a hit from damaging the exposed deployment hardware and making the shot and inventory states visible to the driver. The climb sequence was automated, but the driver described an explicit alliance decision over when to use it.
piece_flow: Deploy the four-bar and compress cargo against the bumper sufficiently to draw it over.
Two powered belts bring off-center cargo toward the tunnel. Two sensors stage and indicate the pair of balls.
Feed a staged ball into the turret shooter after acquiring aim. Wrong or excess cargo can be cleared by the operator.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The deployed pose retracts the cylinder rods into their housings. Shooter and climber shared a mass budget, which forced a shooter redesign. The rotating shooter’s usable cable and hose sweep needs to be plotted separately from the nominal rotation of its ring.

subsystems.name: Collector and bumper crossing
subsystems.construction: Four-bar with pneumatic retraction geometry, wheel contacts, local metal retainers and small anti-pinch flaps.
subsystems.operation: Carry the ball up and over the bumper into the centering belts.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team sought deployed compliance and protection from bending exposed rods. It tuned compression over the bumper.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A sacrificial or compliant front end still needs rigid alignment at the transfer point. Retaining a bearing mechanically is useful where panel flex can push it out.
subsystems.interfaces: The flap must close a trap without introducing a new edge into the ball path.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect screw holes and retention plates after offset hits. Compare corner entry with new and worn bumpers.
subsystems.unknowns: Compression and linkage dimensions are unknown.

subsystems.name: Centering, indexing and feedback
subsystems.construction: Two NEO-driven belts, internal transport wheels, two color sensors and LED strips on the sides.
subsystems.operation: Center the ball, distinguish one and two stored pieces, indicate wrong color and allow operator ejection.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team uses visible signals so the driver can decide without looking away from the field.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Staging only reduces cycle time if the driver can distinguish possession from shooter readiness and knows what a cleared or rejected ball looks like.
subsystems.interfaces: The staging controller must tolerate a partially admitted ball while the belts keep running.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Exercise wrong color, full inventory and intermittent sensor readings. Observe whether the LED signals remain distinguishable from both sides.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact ejection outlet and state code were not reviewed.

subsystems.name: Turret launcher
subsystems.construction: Four printed base quadrants, machined shooter, adjustable hood and two sizes of wheel with different speeds.
subsystems.operation: Use soft targeting for rough tracking and hard lock for acquisition and precision when needed.
subsystems.team_rationale: Weight with the climber drove redesign. The team experimented with wheel hardness and wanted to limit hub bounce-outs.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Separate aiming from launch contact tests. Changing wheel hardness changes contact mechanics even if target tracking is unchanged.
subsystems.interfaces: The hose limits rotation in the description. The next ball has to reach the turret’s entry consistently.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check printed quadrant alignment after a hit and test reacquisition of the correct target after a false lock.
subsystems.unknowns: Verified spin sign, turret range and calibrated speed tables remain open.

subsystems.name: Traversal elevator
subsystems.construction: Elevator, passive latches and pneumatic pivot.
subsystems.operation: Start at mid, take weight on retaining hooks, pivot and catch the next bar, then repeat.
subsystems.team_rationale: A faster prototype was abandoned when the team could not make it work.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Use expected completion value including approach time, partner positions and scoring opportunity forgone.
subsystems.interfaces: The latch must carry load before the elevator changes attitude.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Fixture-test premature release and incomplete pivot with the actual center of mass.
subsystems.unknowns: No proof of a specific field success rate.

revisions: Added retention plates and flaps. Redesigned overweight shooter. Replaced faster climb concept during development.
transferable_principles: Design deployed compliance and protected actuators together.
Separate rough tracking from final shot authorization.
disconfirming_conditions: A stiffer intake can win if compliance causes transfer misalignment.
In playoffs, two reliable traversal partners can raise the value of continuing to score, as the team described.
remaining_gaps: Drive hardware, exact climb tolerances and event-specific configuration.
recommended_images: Request a deployed side view showing the cylinder rod and bumper gap, then an interior view of the tunnel and both sensor locations.
